subject: Initial performance guardrails & streaming cadence — Ava pilot proposals
messages:
From: Megan Ruiz <megan@avasolutions.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: salesops@avasolutions.com
Date: 2026-08-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets + streaming cadence (pilot)

Hi Rohan / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo today — it was helpful to see the streaming behavior end-to-end. Per our internal discussion I wanted to capture our target SLOs and a few constraints so we can make the pilot matrix concrete. Please treat these as starting targets we can refine: 

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target median < 200 ms, p95 < 400 ms for typical 512-token generation (we care most about median).
- Chunk cadence (streaming): for UI smoothness we prefer updates every ~150–300 ms; acceptable chunk sizes are ~50–200 tokens per chunk depending on model.
- Streaming transport: pref SSE by default (simple integration), but must have WebSocket fallback for mobile clients and when we need bidirectional low-latency streams.
- Throughput / concurrency: expected sustained throughput 300 req/s, peak bursts to 700 req/s; concurrent streaming sessions ~150 typical, 300 peak.
- Payloads / prompts: average prompt length ~1.2 KB, worst-case 10 KB. KV cache reuse expected for multi-turn flows.

We have three pilot goals: 1) Verify TTFT under realistic UI pacing, 2) validate chunk cadence & reassembly on our client, 3) measure cost delta between SSE vs WS.

Attachments: I attached our "ava-performance-profile.pdf" that shows sample prompt distributions. Also added a link to our internal pilot folder.

Next steps we see from our side:
- Redwood to propose a short SLO matrix and test harness for the pilot (TTFT probe + burst test).
- Agree on transport defaults (SSE primary, WS fallback) and client reconnection strategy.
- Schedule a 2-hour pilot kickoff next week to exchange test keys and run an initial burst window.

Can you send a quick note with the testing plan and any constraints on model choices / quantization you recommend?

Thanks,

Megan Ruiz
Head of Product
Ava Solutions
megan@avasolutions.com

[Attachment: ava-performance-profile.pdf (summary)]

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Megan Ruiz <megan@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets + streaming cadence (pilot)

Thanks Megan — appreciate the clear targets and the sample distributions. Quick responses inline and a proposed next-step list: 

> - TTFT median < 200 ms, p95 < 400 ms for 512-token generation

This is reasonable for a Hosted/ Dedicated run with an optimized model (FP16/4-bit quantization can help) depending on chosen model family. We'll propose a two-track test: a small-context TTFT probe (single-turn, cached KV) and a full-run probe (cold-start simulating new sessions).

> - Chunk cadence 150–300 ms, SSE preferred with WS fallback

Agree. SSE is simpler to integrate; we'll include a WS fallback in the pilot plan. For SSE we recommend chunk framing that includes a small preface header (chunk_id, seq, partial_output_flag) so your client reassembly is deterministic.

> - Throughput / concurrency: sustained 300 req/s, bursts to 700 req/s; concurrent sessions ~150 / 300 peak

Good to know. For bursts we typically recommend a short warm-up (30–60s) and a burst-shaping policy in Redwood to avoid cold starts at the worst times. We'll size the pilot to run a 10-minute sustained burst to observe degradation modes.

Proposed immediate deliverables from Redwood: 
- Pilot matrix (attachment) covering probe types, metrics to collect (TTFT p50/p95/p99, chunk interval distribution, bytes/chunk, error rate), and pass/fail thresholds.
- Test harness endpoints (SSE and WS) + keys.
- Suggested model candidates (one smaller low-latency quantized model + one higher-quality model) and estimated cost per 1k tokens for each.

I've attached a draft pilot-matrix.xlsx (stub) that we can refine in the kickoff. Proposed kickoff windows: Tue 2026-08-25 14:00-16:00 PT or Thu 2026-08-27 09:00-11:00 PT. Which works for you?

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com
[Attachment: pilot-matrix.xlsx (stub)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Ruiz <megan@avasolutions.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets + streaming cadence (pilot)

Looping in a couple of ops notes from infra POV. Few recommendations and constraints to include in the pilot doc: 

- Transport choice: WebSocket gives slightly lower jitter under high concurrency and allows bi-directional health pings. If you expect mobile clients with flaky networks, plan to test both; we'll instrument both paths, but start with SSE for simplicity.
- Chunk cadence measurement: instrument emit timestamps in server logs (epoch ms) and include them in pilot metrics. We'll compute inter-chunk deltas and CDFs.
- TTFT probe: include two flavors — 1) cold-start (no KV cache), 2) hot (with KV reuse). Expect ~2–3x worse TTFT for cold-start on long-context models.
- Kernel selection & quantization: for the low-latency track we recommend an int4 path where possible + attention kernels tuned to your max context length; I'll include recommended kernel profiles in the pilot doc.

Operational ask: please confirm your max context length and tokenization choices (we need the max tokens to choose kernels). Also confirm whether you want request-level tracing enabled (adds ~5–8 ms overhead but is invaluable for root-cause).

I left a draft pilot checklist in the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AvaPilotPlan — includes a sample tracing toggle and buffering parameters.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Megan Ruiz <megan@avasolutions.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets + streaming cadence (pilot)

Thanks — this is great detail and the proposed plan makes sense. Quick answers: 

- Max context length: 4096 tokens for our longest multi-turn flows; tokenization is standard UTF-8 whitespace-based with some special markers, average token size aligns with the attached profile.
- Tracing: yes, enable request-level tracing for the pilot (we'll accept the small overhead).
- Transport: SSE primary + WS fallback — we'll test both. For mobile, WS fallback is functionally required.
- Kickoff: Tue 2026-08-25 14:00-16:00 PT works for our team.

A few asks for the kickoff agenda:
1) Keys & endpoints handoff
2) Quick run of the cold TTFT probe (5–10 min)
3) Burst test (10 min at 700 req/s)
4) Chunk cadence validation on our client (visual check + metrics)
5) Next steps & timeline for a 2-week pilot

On cost: can you include an estimated per-1k-token cost for SSE vs WS scenarios and any overhead for tracing? We'll evaluate against our budget and circle back.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Megan Ruiz
Head of Product, Ava Solutions
megan@avasolutions.com
